stances.claim: The Pulido en banc holding correctly allows an accused in a bigamy prosecution to invoke the void-ab-initio nullity of the prior marriage as a defense even without a prior judicial declaration of nullity -- though such declaration remains required for civil-effects purposes (remarriage, heirship, legitimacy, property regimes).
stances.rhetorical_move: agreement with holding + clarification of remaining scope
stances.confidence: asserted with the Court's own bolded language

stances.claim: The Family Code's PI ground was copied from Canon Law with no prior constitutional, statutory, or jurisprudential precedent -- making canonical concepts (gravity, juridical antecedence, incurability) the only sensible starting point, as Santos and Molina recognized.
stances.rhetorical_move: originalist-source framing (the doctrine's canonical pedigree is constitutive, not optional)

stances.claim: Tan-Andal's abandonment of the Santos/Molina guidelines and elimination of the expert-evidence requirement makes the new PI proceedings 'strikingly similar to absolute divorce in many jurisdictions' -- functionally producing divorce without legislative authorization.
stances.rhetorical_move: functional-equivalence critique (judicial circumvention of legislative non-action)

stances.claim: The Court should have waited for Congress to legislate absolute divorce if that be the sovereign will, rather than 'mangling the canonical PI' to achieve the same effect by doctrinal modification.
stances.rhetorical_move: separation-of-powers critique (defer to legislature on policy)
stances.confidence: asserted as alternative path with rhetorical question

stances.claim: Religious-school alumni jurists who joined Tan-Andal should examine whether the result is consistent with the institutional creeds they invoked (St. Thomas More, amDg, Ora et labora, Veritas) -- a question CJ poses but, as a nonsectarian-school alum, declines to answer.
stances.rhetorical_move: shame-by-creed (calling alumni jurists to apply their schools' mottos to their own ruling)
stances.confidence: framed as deferred judgment ('Let them judge the judges; I dare not')

notable_anecdotes: Pulido facts: Luisito was a 16-year-old student in 1983 marrying his 22-year-old teacher Nora; he later contracted a second marriage with Rowena in 1995; Nora filed bigamy in 2007; RTC convicted in 2009 -- but the second marriage was independently declared void by another RTC after the conviction, raising the chicken-and-egg question Pulido resolved.
Santos v. CA traced PI's three canonical characteristics -- gravity, juridical antecedence, incurability -- directly to the Family Code's lift from Canon Law.

Molina relied on amicus curiae Archbishop Oscar V. Cruz, presiding judge of the Church's National Appellate Matrimonial Tribunal -- making the Church the formal doctrinal authority on PI's civil application.

Tan-Andal denounced Santos and Molina as 'restrictive, rigid, and intrusive on our rights to liberty, autonomy, and human dignity' -- Justice Leonen's ponencia attracted 9 separate concurring opinions, a high-conviction unanimity gesture.

Roll call of school mottos: Atenean 'amDg' (Ad majorem Dei gloriam -- to the greater glory of God), Bedan 'Ora et labora' (pray and work), Thomasian 'Veritas' (truth), UP's 'Be brave' -- with CJ as 'just a humble offspring of the Be brave tradition of a nonsectarian university that does not have an incumbent member of the Court.'
Closing rhetorical question with two options: (a) consistency with St. Thomas More's 'the King's good servant but God's first,' (b) defer to Congress to legislate absolute divorce.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban opens with the Family Code Article 40 puzzle -- whether an accused can be acquitted of bigamy without a prior judicial declaration of the first marriage's nullity -- and reports that the Supreme Court answered YES en banc in Pulido v. People (July 27, 2021), penned by Justice Hernando with three separate concurring opinions, using the chicken-and-egg facts of Luisito (a 16-year-old who married his 22-year-old teacher Nora in 1983, then Rowena in 1995, was convicted of bigamy in 2009, and saw the second marriage independently declared void shortly after). The judicial declaration is now required only 'for purposes of remarriage' and for civil-rights determinations (heirship, legitimacy, estates, property regimes). The column then pivots to Psychological Incapacity, tracing its doctrinal arc from Santos v. CA (1995) -- which adopted the canonical characteristics of gravity, juridical antecedence, and incurability -- through Republic v. Molina (1997), whose guidelines were sourced from amicus Archbishop Oscar V. Cruz of the Church's National Appellate Matrimonial Tribunal, to Tan-Andal v. Andal (May 11, 2021), Justice Leonen's unanimous ponencia (with nine separate concurring opinions) that denounced Santos and Molina as 'restrictive, rigid, and intrusive on our rights to liberty, autonomy, and human dignity' and eliminated the expert-evidence requirement. In CJ's IMHO, the resulting proceedings are 'strikingly similar to absolute divorce in many jurisdictions,' and he poses a pointed shame-by-creed question to the religious-school alumni jurists who joined Tan-Andal: is the result consistent with St. Thomas More's 'the King's good servant but God's first,' with the Atenean 'amDg,' the Bedan 'Ora et labora,' and the Thomasian 'Veritas'? As 'just a humble offspring of the Be brave tradition of a nonsectarian university that does not have an incumbent member of the Court,' he declines to answer and closes by asking whether the Court should instead have waited for Congress to legislate absolute divorce -- if that be the sovereign will -- rather than mangling the canonical PI doctrine to achieve the same effect.
